basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens 'Vers. 21. Tolles de omnibus escis. Hoc loco quaeritur de animalibus quae carnibus'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 21. Tolles de omnibus escis. Hoc loco quaeritur de animalibus quae carnibus vescuntur, quomodo in arca anno integro vixerint, cum carnes tanto tempore incorruptae servari non potuerint. Ad hoc dicendum quia sunt quaedam animalia quae carnibus vescuntur, sed si necessitas imperaverit, fructibus et pomis diversi generis vivere possunt, maxime ficu et castanea.
